title: fmole: prompts, repulsive core, missing template
purpose: Exercises further `fmole` paths [@epsrmanual]: the file name and number of shakes typed on stdin, the intramolecular repulsive core potential switched on through the `ecore dcore` line of the `.ato` file, and a molecule whose template file is missing. This complements the standard route of ex33 for the geometry relaxation used before EPSR runs [@soper2005].
fortran: `fmole.f`: `fmole` (stdin prompts), `initpt_fmole`, `update_ato` (template cannot be opened: bonds kept)
system: Single molecules of the EPSR-test system [@soperluzar1992] at 300 K: one dimethyl sulphoxide molecule (10 atoms, box 21.544 Å) and one water molecule (3 atoms, box 14.422 Å). In `DMSOcore.ato` the `ecore dcore` line is set to 0.3 2.5 (instead of 0 0), so the repulsive Weeks-Chandler-Andersen-type core of `generate_mp` [@wca1971] acts on the non-bonded H...H pairs in addition to the harmonic bond and angle restraints.
inputs: `DMSO.ato` from EPSR-test; `DMSOcore.ato` = `DMSO.ato` with `ecore dcore = 0.3 2.5` (the only changed line); `Water.ato` = `WaterMolecule.ato` renamed, so its template is absent. Commands: `fmole < fmole1.stdin` (file `DMSOcore` typed — no listing — and 150 shakes asked on stdin) and `fmole Water < fmole2.stdin` (30 shakes); `update_ato` cannot open the template and keeps the bonds of the file.
verification: Two program calls in one pass; compared outputs: the rewritten `DMSOcore.ato` and `Water.ato` and the empty `dirlist.txt`, identical including coordinates and the random-number state.
